query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Setting the HVAF‐i7 nozzle-to-substrate spray distance to 300–350 mm will increase particle acceleration and kinetic energy, leading to improved splat flattening and inter-splat bonding, ultimately overcoming the thickness limitation while preserving low oxidation and coating integrity.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with a 15–45 μm size distribution, as currently used in HVAF‐i7 deposition on confined components (internal diameters as small as 120 mm).
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF‐i7 process by increasing the spray distance to 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition under an inert atmosphere using the HVAF‐i7 torch on substrates or components with internal diameters as small as 120 mm; all other parameters (e.g., gas flow, feedstock composition) remain consistent with the baseline process.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced in‐flight particle acceleration leads to a higher impact momentum, promoting better splat deformation and inter-splat adhesion.
generation.mechanism: By extending the spray distance, particles have more time to accelerate within the jet flow. This results in increased kinetic energy upon impact, which improves the flattening and bonding of individual splats. The inert atmosphere limits oxidation, so the improved deposition efficiency translates into a thicker, adherent coating capable of withstanding high-temperature service.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under the increased spray distance conditions, the deposition efficiency is expected to improve, resulting in a bond coat that is significantly thicker than the baseline HVAF‐i7 deposition while maintaining low levels of as-sprayed oxidation and ensuring durability during thermal-barrier service.
generation.baseline: The baseline is HVAF‐i7 deposition using a 15–45 μm feedstock at the standard (shorter) spray distance, which yields acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: The intervention should remain effective on components with internal diameters down to 120 mm and under deposition conditions that continue to provide an inert atmosphere. It is also contingent on maintaining other process parameters (e.g., gas flow and feed rate) at levels similar to the baseline setup.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in thickness and its correlation with mechanical and oxidation-resistant properties remain to be determined. There is also some uncertainty regarding the potential impact on microstructural features when modifying the spray distance, which requires further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of controlled deposition experiments using the HVAF‐i7 torch. Compare coatings produced using the standard spray distance (baseline) and an extended spray distance of 300–350 mm, using identical 15–45 μm feedstock and deposition conditions on substrates representing internal diameters of 120 mm.
measurements: Adhesion strength (assessed by standardized pull-off adhesion tests)
Oxidation levels (analyzed using XPS or EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the specimens deposited at 300–350 mm do not exhibit statistically significant improvement in coating thickness, or if they show reduced adhesion or increased levels of oxidation compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis that the increased spray distance overcomes the thickness limitation will be falsified.

proposals.intervention: Optimize the HVAF‐i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm to increase particle velocity during deposition
proposals.conditions: Use the HVAF‐i7 torch with current 15–45 μm feedstock in coating chambers including internal diameters as small as 120 mm; set the nozzle-to-substrate distance to 300–350 mm at conventional gas flow settings
proposals.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle flattening and splat formation
proposals.mechanism: The increased spray distance permits particles more time to accelerate under the HVAF‐i7 jet, thereby raising kinetic energy on impact. This improved flattening and bonding leads to higher deposition efficiency and thicker, more adherent coatings with limited oxidation since the in‐flight oxidization remains controlled by the inert gas environment
proposals.predicted_outcome: Coatings deposited at 300–350 mm will exhibit significantly increased thickness (relative to the baseline from the standard HVAF‐i7 settings) while retaining coating integrity and low oxidation, ensuring durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single parameter change employs the established beneficial effect seen in conventional MCrAlY coatings using the M3 system—where optimal spray distances enhanced deposition efficiency—thus directly targeting the thickness limitation observed with HVAF‐i7

proposals.intervention: Tailor the feedstock particle size distribution by incorporating a fraction of larger particles (e.g., 30–70 μm) while maintaining a mixed size population
proposals.conditions: Utilize the HVAF‐i7 torch with a modified feedstock blend in which the conventional 15–45 μm range is supplemented with 30–70 μm particles, deposited at standard spray distances inside 120 mm internal diameter components
proposals.structural_mediator: Increased particle momentum and improved inter‐splat impact energies
proposals.mechanism: Larger particles possess greater momentum on impact, enabling improved deformation and bonding. This mechanism enhances deposition efficiency and layer build-up, leading to thicker coatings. Although oxidation risks must be managed, the in-flight conditions of HVAF (inert atmosphere and short dwell times) keep oxidation low
proposals.predicted_outcome: The modified feedstock will yield a thicker, adherent bond coat compared to the baseline 15–45 μm feedstock, with reduced porosity and maintained oxidation resistance
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By modifying the particle power input through size distribution adjustment, the deposition process overcomes the thickness limitation without sacrificing the coating’s mechanical and oxidation-resistant properties established in earlier studies

proposals.intervention: Enhance gas flow and feedstock injection rate parameters in the HVAF‐i7 process
proposals.conditions: Operate the HVAF‐i7 torch in a configuration where gas flow rates and feedstock injection rates are incrementally increased; maintain the same 15–45 μm feedstock and deposition in confined geometries (e.g., 120 mm diameters)
proposals.structural_mediator: Increased particle velocity and momentum flux leading to improved splat adhesion and layering
proposals.mechanism: By augmenting gas flow and injection rates, the particles are accelerated to higher velocities, which enhances their kinetic energy upon impact. This results in superior adhesion and more efficient layering, thereby enabling the buildup of thicker coatings while limiting as-sprayed oxidation due to the protective gas environment
proposals.predicted_outcome: A marked improvement in deposition thickness relative to the baseline HVAF‐i7 setting will be observed, and the resultant bond coats should retain structural integrity under high-temperature service
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach directly tackles the inadequate deposition thickness by focusing on process parameter optimization that has shown deposition efficiency improvements in related systems, as evidenced in the conventional MCrAlY studies

proposals.intervention: Introduce controlled in-situ substrate preheating and inter-pass reheating during deposition
proposals.conditions: Implement a protocol in the HVAF‐i7 process where substrates are preheated (e.g., 200–300°C) and short dwell-time reheating cycles (maintaining similar temperatures) are applied between successive deposition passes, using the standard 15–45 μm feedstock within 120 mm internal diameters
proposals.structural_mediator: Enhanced splat coalescence and inter-layer metallurgical bonding
proposals.mechanism: Preheating reduces the thermal gradients upon impact, facilitating better plastic deformation and fusion between splats. The inter-pass reheating ensures that deposited layers partially remelt or sinter at their contact interfaces, thus building a thicker, more integrated coating with fewer interfacial defects and low as-sprayed oxidation
proposals.predicted_outcome: The resulting bond coat will be significantly thicker and exhibit enhanced adhesion and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, surpassing the baseline performance while retaining low oxidation levels
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By promoting inter-splat bonding during deposition, this intervention directly addresses the limitation in coating thickness through an alternate mechanism that complements the kinetic improvements provided by HVAF spraying, ensuring service durability in confined geometries

decision.rationale: Direction C leverages established process optimization in conventional MCrAlY coatings, where a nozzle-to-substrate distance of 300–350 mm produced higher particle velocities and improved deposition efficiency. This directly targets the thickness limitation observed with the HVAF‐i7 torch while using the existing 15–45 μm feedstock. The cited studies provide evidence that increased spray distance yields enhanced particle flattening and splat formation, and no fatal objections were noted with this approach.
